did.abstract: Asian Women in Business (AWIB) was a non-profit organization founded by Bonnie Wong in 1985 that worked to increase the number of women- and minority-owned businesses by providing resources and support for Asian women entrepreneurs. AWIB hosted courses designed to help small businesses and sponsored annual corporate leadership conferences to provide minority and women entrepreneurs opportunities to establish relationships with corporate and government entities. To encourage young Asian women to attend college and assume leadership positions, AWIB also awarded annual academic scholarships. At its peak, AWIB had hundreds of members, and functioned as the only Asian women's business association of its time. The Asian Women in Business Records (dated 1995-2018) consists of materials documenting the administrative activities and programming of AWIB, and includes photographs, flyers and brochures, records of programs and conferences, annual reports within anniversary gathering programs, and newspaper clippings in English, Chinese, and Korean. The collection also includes a small amount of documentation of AWIB's nonprofit status. Materials document the day-to-day activities of AWIB, as well as its role as a networking hub, outreach advocate, community partner, and center for developing business leaders.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Asian Women in Business Records (dated 1995-2018) consists of materials documenting the administrative activities and programming of Asian Women in Business (AWIB). Materials include photographs, flyers and brochures, records of programs and conferences, annual reports within anniversary gathering programs, and newspaper clippings in English, Chinese, and Korean. The collection also includes a small amount of documentation of AWIB's nonprofit status. Materials document the day-to-day activities of AWIB, as well as its role as a networking hub, outreach advocate, community partner, and center for developing business leaders.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Materials are arranged alphabetically, with programming documentation in chronological order.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: Asian Women in Business (AWIB) was a non-profit organization founded by Bonnie Wong in 1985 that worked to increase the number of women- and minority-owned businesses by providing resources and support for Asian women entrepreneurs. AWIB hosted courses designed to help small businesses and sponsored annual corporate leadership conferences to provide minority and women entrepreneurs opportunities to establish relationships with corporate and government entities. Programming examples include the Procurement Opportunities Conference, Asian Women's Corporate Leadership Conference, "Taste of Chinatown," and the Leadership Awards Ceremony and Dinner. To encourage young Asian women to attend college and assume leadership positions, AWIB also awarded annual academic scholarships. After the September 11, 2001 attacks on the World Trade Center, AWIB was awarded several grants to help bring businesses back to Chinatown in lower Manhattan. AWIB staff also went door-to-door offering business owners technical assistance and other resources. At its peak, AWIB had hundreds of members, and functioned as the only Asian women's business association of its time. Wong's background was working in civil rights and government policy. She created AWIB after recognizing the lack of professional development space and community gathering for Asian women in the fields of business and entrepreneurship.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: At the time of accessioning, materials were removed from their original binders and rehoused in archival boxes and folders, maintaining original groupings of materials. Materials were described on the collection-level with a folder-level inventory. All folder titles are original to the donor. Significant portions of the archival description in this guide were modified from a survey report completed by Daniella Occhineri in their capacity as a Graduate Archives Scholar with the A/P/A Institute.
